_comment: Templates per workspace. The five default templates (welcome-diner, order-confirmed, order-ready, order-receipt, sign-in-alert) are IDENTICAL in both workspaces — sample data included — because every customer of the platform is a restaurant chain running the same core notifications; only the per-customer additions differ. Default copy stays neutral across dine-in, pickup and delivery: order-ready's payload ({{handoff_note}}) says where to collect the order or that it is on its way, so the workflow assumes neither, and delivery language lives only in Nolan's arriving-soon. Email bodies are NOT stored here — they live as a visual-designer pair at suprsend/templates/<ws>/<slug>/email/default/body.designer.{html,json}, generated by scripts/make-designs.mjs from the `heading`/`paragraph`/`button` fields below. Run make-designs before provision.mjs templates. Subjects use TRIPLE-stache ({{{var}}}): Handlebars' {{var}} HTML-escapes its output, which is right inside the HTML body but wrong in a plain-text subject line — with {{$brand.brand_name}} a subject reads Nolan's / Ember & Oak. Body fields keep {{var}}, where escaping is correct. Templates render brand fields as {{$brand.*}} — SuprSend's docs have since renamed brands to tenants and document {{$tenant.*}}, which resolves to the same object; this app migrates later, so keep {{$brand.*}} and change no template variables. Per-recipient values must come from {{$recipient.*}}: broadcast `data` is identical for every recipient, so {{$recipient.name}} is the only safe way to personalise a broadcast. The welcome template carries NO sampleData on purpose: its workflow is triggered by list entry, and $USER_ENTERED_LIST is emitted by SuprSend rather than by this app, so there is no payload to fill custom variables from. It templates on $recipient and $brand only. order-feedback is variable-free for a similar reason: it shares its ORDER_COMPLETED trigger with order-receipt, so it must render from whatever payload the receipt event carries — the safe set is none. Anything needing per-send values must be triggered by an event this app emits, or sent as a broadcast. A template with `broadcastCategory` can be sent as a broadcast, under that category — SuprSend templates carry no category of their own and a broadcast has to name one, so the seed records it here. The category must be promotional (a broadcast on a transactional or system category holds up that category's other traffic) and it is not a per-send choice, since the category decides whose opt-outs apply. Templates without it are still perfectly sendable — by a workflow, which names its own category, and which is where a template carrying per-send variables belongs: a broadcast has one payload for everyone, so broadcasting such a template would send one recipient's details to the whole list.
